description: The server assigns the session ID; the create request carries none.

input.step: alice creates a session over POST, with no session ID anywhere

notes: session_id is server-generated and unguessable (at least 128 bits). The harness captures it as {{sid}} for later steps.

description: A create request that proposes a session ID is refused.

input.step: create with a client-chosen session_id in the wmp metadata
create with a client-chosen Wmp-Session-Id header

notes: No session exists under ses-chosen-by-client afterwards: a GET for it is the same 404 as for any unknown session.

description: An event stream request without credentials is answered 401.
A session owned by someone else and a session that does not exist give the same response.

input.step: bob asks for a session that does not exist

notes: Status, headers other than Date, and body are identical. A POST for either gives the same JSON-RPC error -31000.

description: Every event carries an id; ids are strictly ordered by emission.

input.step: server emits two notifications before any stream is open
alice opens a stream with no cursor: nothing is replayed

notes: Ids are opaque: the harness only captures them and checks that they are distinct; it never assumes they are numeric or contiguous. Their ordering is exercised by the replay vectors that follow. A stream with no cursor starts at the next event.

description: Reconnect with the Last-Event-ID header replays exactly the events after the cursor.

input.step: server emits one more: delivered live after the replay, with a new id

notes: The event the cursor names (e2) is not sent again. Replayed events keep their original ids.

description: The last_event_id query parameter works when the header cannot be set.
When both forms are present the header is the cursor.

input.step: alice reconnects with Last-Event-ID = e4 and last_event_id = e1

description: A cursor at the newest event replays nothing.
A cursor whose next event is still in the buffer is not a gap.

input.step: server emits five notifications; the buffer keeps the newest three (e3, e4, e5)
alice reconnects with Last-Event-ID = e2: e3 is the oldest retained event

notes: Buffer of three events. The boundary is the event after the cursor, not the cursor itself.

description: A cursor whose next event was evicted is a gap: 410, then the client resumes.

input.step: server emits five notifications; the buffer keeps the newest three (e3, e4, e5)
alice reconnects with Last-Event-ID = e1: e2 was evicted
the client discards its cursor and resumes the session
then opens a stream with no cursor: no replay, no 410

notes: {{rt}} is the resumption_token of the create result. The server MUST NOT send any part of the replay with the 410.

description: A cursor the server never issued for this session is a gap.

input.step: alice opens a stream with a cursor that was never issued

notes: Evicted, never issued and discarded buffers are not distinguishable, so all give 410.

description: An idle stream receives comment-line heartbeats that carry no id.

input.step: alice opens a stream and stays idle for 35 seconds
server emits one notification: the cursor is that event's id, not a heartbeat's
alice reconnects with Last-Event-ID = e1: nothing to replay

notes: Comment lines begin with ':' and are not WMP messages. The harness advances its (simulated) clock; it does not sleep.

description: The live completion carries the secrets; the replayed copy omits them and says so.

input.step: server emits the completion; the streaming connection gets the live copy
alice reconnects with Last-Event-ID = e1: the replayed completion is redacted

notes: wmp-openid4x Section 3.1.4.2. The retained copy never held the secret members; the replayed copy keeps the live copy's id, so a client that already processed the live one dedupes it.
